name: Question 5
worked_solution:
Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form $\frac{0}{0},$ as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (2,1,-1)}\frac{y+z}{\sqrt{x-y}-\sqrt{x+z}} & =\frac{1+(-1)}{\sqrt{2-1}-\sqrt{2+(-1)}} \\  & =\frac{1-1}{1-1} \\  & =\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

However, we can simplify the limit by first multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (2,1,-1)}\frac{y+z}{\sqrt{x-y}-\sqrt{x+z}} & ={lim}_{x\to (2,1,-1)}\frac{(y+z)(\sqrt{x-y}+\sqrt{x+z})}{(\sqrt{x-y}-\sqrt{x+z})(\sqrt{x-y}+\sqrt{x+z})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (2,1,-1)}\frac{(y+z)(\sqrt{x-y}+\sqrt{x+z})}{(x-y)-(x+z)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to (2,1,-1)}\frac{(y+z)(\sqrt{x-y}+\sqrt{x+z})}{-(y+z)} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to (2,1,-1)}\frac{\cancel{(y+z)}(\sqrt{x-y}+\sqrt{x+z})}{\cancel{(y+z)}} \\  & =-{lim}_{x\to (2,1,-1)}(\sqrt{x-y}+\sqrt{x+z})\end{aligned}
$$

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it:

$$
\begin{aligned}-{lim}_{x\to (2,1,-1)}(\sqrt{x-y}+\sqrt{x+z}) & =-(\sqrt{2-1}+\sqrt{2+(-1)}) \\  & =-(1+1) \\  & =-2\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the limit evaluates to $-2.$

EXPLANATION

Attempting to evaluate the limit by direct substitution leads to the indeterminate form 00, as follows: limx→(2,1,−1)y+zx−y−x+z=1+(−1)2−1−2+(−1)=1−11−1=00

However, we can simplify the limit by first multiplying the numerator and denominator by the conjugate of the denominator: limx→(2,1,−1)y+zx−y−x+z=limx→(2,1,−1)(y+z)(x−y+x+z)(x−y−x+z)(x−y+x+z)=limx→(2,1,−1)(y+z)(x−y+x+z)(x−y)−(x+z)=limx→(2,1,−1)(y+z)(x−y+x+z)−(y+z)=−limx→(2,1,−1)(y+z)(x−y+x+z)(y+z)=−limx→(2,1,−1)(x−y+x+z)

Now that the limit has been simplified, we can evaluate it: −limx→(2,1,−1)(x−y+x+z)=−(2−1+2+(−1))=−(1+1)=−2

Therefore, the limit evaluates to −2.
